FR0000121014.title: LVMH: Accelerating growth in the second quarter; solid first-half results
FR0000121014.start:
Accelerating growth in the second quarter
Solid first-half results
. Revenue: €38.6 billion
. Profit from recurring operations: €8.7 billion
. Free cash flow: €4.1 billion
Paris, July 27, 2026
LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton, the world’s leading high-quality products group, recorded revenue
of €38.6 billion in the first half of 2026. LVMH maintained its innovative momentum and remained very
solid in a geopolitical and economic environment that remained disrupted, amplified by the conflict in the
Middle East. Growth accelerated in the second quarter, with organic revenue growth for the Group of 3%
(4% excluding the impact of the conflict in the Middle East).
The United States saw growth accelerate and had a good first half of the year. Asia (excluding Japan) saw
strong growth, confirming the improvement in trends observed starting in the second half of 2025. Japan
posted growth for the half-year period and Europe showed good resilience.
Profit from recurring operations for the first half of 2026 came to €8.7 billion, equating to an operating
margin that remained high at 22.5%. The Group share of net profit amounted to €5.7 billion, stable year
on year.
Bernard Arnault, Chairman and CEO of LVMH, commented: “LVMH demonstrated its solidity and
effective strategy. Our Maisons – which remained focused on ensuring the utmost quality in our products,
and several of which are pursuing their creative renewal – continued to inspire dreams and enhance their
desirability. Accelerating growth in the second quarter arose in particular from the success of Jonathan
Anderson’s first designs for Christian Dior, the remarkable performance of Louis Vuitton’s exceptional
new stores in Beijing and Seoul, and Tiffany and Bvlgari’s iconic lines. Strong growth at Sephora and the
recovery in champagne and cognac also contributed to this excellent momentum. While continuing to pay
very close attention to margins, we are entering the second half of the year with renewed confidence in
the long-term potential of our Maisons and in our highly committed teams to continue to stand out and
reinforce LVMH’s leadership position. The latest edition of our Journées Particulières events will
showcase the invaluable expertise of our craftspeople and the rich heritage of our Maisons, offering an
array of unique experiences.”
Highlights of the first half of 2026 included the following:
• Solid results over the half-year period.
• Accelerating growth in the second quarter.
• Growth in profit from recurring operations excluding the negative currency impact.
• High level of operating margin maintained at 22.5%.
• Robust cash flow of €4.1 billion.
• Signs of recovery for Wines & Spirits.
• Gradual acceleration in Fashion & Leather Goods, which returned to organic revenue growth in the
second quarter.
• Excellent performance in jewelry for Tiffany and Bvlgari.
• Sustained growth at Sephora.1/11

PRESS RELEASE
Third quarter 2026 results
TotalEnergies is leveraging once again its integrated business model
and geographic diversification to post adjusted net income of $9.1 billion
and cash flow of $12.3 billion, a sharp increase quarter-to-quarter
• Gearing reached below 10% by the end of the third quarter 2026
• New capital increase reserved for employees at a 20% discount on the share price
• Interim dividend maintained at €0.90/share
• $2.5 billion share buybacks in 4th quarter 2026 and in 1st quarter 2027
1
Paris, October 29, 2026 – The Board of Directors of TotalEnergies SE, chaired by CEO Patrick Pouyanné,
met on October 28, 2026, to approve the 3rd quarter 2026 financial statements. On the occasion, Patrick
Pouyanné said:
“In a high-price environment characterized by historic refining margin levels and a bull gas market, TotalEnergies is
once again fully leveraging its integrated business model and its geographic diversification by posting an adjusted net
income of $9.1 billion and cash flow of $12.3 billion for the third quarter, a sharp increase quarter-to-quarter.
Oil & Gas production reached 2.474 Mboe/d in the third quarter, up more than 3% quarter-to-quarter, notably benefiting
from a lower impact of the Middle East conflict, limited to only around 5% of the Company’s overall production over
the quarter on average. Excluding the Middle East impact, production growth exceeds 4% year-on-year, supported by
the ramp-up of projects launched since 2025. Furthermore, with the investment decisions taken this quarter for Cronos
in Cyprus, Ima in Nigeria, Umm Shaif Gas Cap in the United Arab Emirates and Absheron Ph2 in Azerbaijan, all the
projects contributing to achieving the production growth target of more than 3% per year by 2030 are now in execution
phase.
Exploration and Production posted adjusted net operating income of $3.2 billion and cash flow of $5.4 billion, reflecting
production growth, sensitivity to declining oil prices and rising gas prices quarter-to-quarter. The Company completed
its entry into PEL83 license holding the Mopane discovery and took part in three exploration discoveries in Norway
(Grimsnes) and in Angola (Block 0 and Block 17 – Violeta 4). TotalEnergies once again demonstrates its leadership
to control costs, with operating costs of $4.7/boe, anchored below $5/boe.
The Integrated LNG segment achieved adjusted net operating income of $1.9 billion and cash flow of $1.7 billion in
the third quarter of 2026, a very sharp increase quarter-to-quarter, underpinned by a 20% increase in average LNG
price and the outperformance of LNG and gas trading activities in a bull market.

SANTA CLARA and REDWOOD CITY, Calif. – August 17, 2026 – NVIDIA announced that it has secured land, power and shell (LPS) capacity through a partnership with SB Energy at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio, to host NVIDIA compute. OpenAI will be the customer. SB Energy will build, own and operate the data center under a 20-year lease to OpenAI.

Demand for AI is growing at an extraordinary pace. AI is becoming infrastructure, requiring a full stack of critical resources, including LPS. To meet this moment, NVIDIA is securing the LPS capacity at PORTS-Pike to exclusively host NVIDIA AI factories. This unique campus development will lay the foundation for tomorrow’s breakthroughs, enabling communities to drive scientific discovery, health care advances and regional economic development.

OpenAI will utilize the capacity at the site. The AI factory will use NVIDIA’s full-stack DSX AI factory platform, including GPUs, CPUs and networking. The initial deployment is designed to support 4.25 IT-GW of AI factory capacity. NVIDIA has the option to extend the opportunity at PORTS-Pike beyond the initial capacity. The DSX AI factory architecture used at PORTS-Pike will deliver resiliency across the full stack – facilities, hardware, and software together – reducing infrastructure overhead and accelerating time to tokens for the next generation of AI factories.

“AI is becoming infrastructure – the foundation for intelligence in every industry – and land, power and shell have become vital in the age of AI. cyclical shocks.

and Ryanair to Southern Europe. Belgrade airport confirmed its dynamism and role as a regional hub, with
strong performance on routes to Western Europe. At Edinburgh airport, traffic growth this quarter was driven
by increased capacity from airlines such as Ryanair, easyJet, and Jet2, particularly to Mediterranean
destinations. In Portugal, strong performance continued: Porto and Faro stood out, with significant
increases in passenger numbers this quarter (respectively +7.1% and +3.7%).
In the Cabo Verde archipelago, airports recorded a notable increase in traffic driven by the strengthening of
connections with Europe, in particular through new routes operated by easyJet and TAP.
In Mexico, traffic growth was driven this quarter by strong domestic flights between regional airports.
Meanwhile, Salvador Bahia airport in Brazil confirmed its rise as a regional hub following investments by
the airline GOL. In the Caribbean, Dominican Republic airports saw significant growth thanks to connections
with Spain, other islands in the region, and Latin America.
Conversely, geopolitical disruptions continued to impact traffic at some airports. In Asia, tensions between
China and Japan again weighed on the trends of Japanese airports in the network (-8.8%). In this context,
Cambodia also recorded a decline in traffic, linked to decreased demand from China and Thailand. In Chile,
